examples.ko: 그 이야기는 너무 관념적이라서 잘 와닿지 않아요.
examples.en: That story is so abstract that it doesn't really connect with me.

examples.ko: 관념적인 설명보다 구체적인 예를 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please give a concrete example rather than an abstract explanation.
If you only think of love in the abstract, real life gets hard.

examples.ko: 이 소설은 내용이 관념적이어서 읽기가 어려워요.
examples.en: This novel is hard to read because its content is so abstract.

examples.ko: 우리 팀장님은 말이 관념적일 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Our team leader's talk is often abstract.

examples.ko: 평화에 대한 관념적 논의만 계속하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: We shouldn't keep having only abstract discussions about peace.

explain: '추상적'과 비슷하지만 '관념적'은 현실과 떨어져 머릿속 생각에만 머문다는 부정적인 느낌이 자주 있어요. 반대말은 '현실적', '구체적'이에요. '관념적인 이야기', '관념적이다'처럼 '인'이나 '이다'를 붙여 써요.
explain_en: It is close to '추상적' (abstract), but '관념적' often carries a negative feel of staying in the head and being detached from reality. Its opposites are '현실적' and '구체적'. It is used like '관념적인 이야기' or '관념적이다', with '인' or '이다' attached.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 오랜 경력에서 나오는 관록이 느껴져요.
examples.en: You can feel the gravitas that comes from that actor's long career.

examples.ko: 관록 있는 감독이 팀을 맡아서 든든해요.
examples.en: It's reassuring that a seasoned coach is leading the team.

examples.ko: 신인인데도 관록 있는 연기를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: Even though she's a newcomer, she gave a performance with real poise.

examples.ko: 관록이 붙은 선수라서 큰 경기에서도 침착해요.
examples.en: He's an experienced player, so he stays calm even in big games.

examples.ko: 그 식당 주인은 관록이 묻어나는 솜씨로 요리해요.
examples.en: The restaurant owner cooks with a skill that shows years of experience.

examples.ko: 아직 관록은 부족하지만 열심히 하고 있어요.
examples.en: I still lack the weight of experience, but I'm working hard.

explain: 오랜 경험에서 나오는 여유와 무게감을 말해서 사람이나 솜씨를 칭찬할 때 써요. '관록이 있다', '관록이 붙다', '관록이 느껴지다'처럼 자주 말해요. 경력이 쌓인 사람에게 쓰는 말이라 갓 시작한 사람에게는 어울리지 않아요.
explain_en: It describes the ease and weight that come from long experience, so you use it to praise a person or their skill. Common patterns are '관록이 있다', '관록이 붙다' and '관록이 느껴지다'. It suits people with accumulated experience, not someone who has just started.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 일 처리가 너무 관료적이에요.
examples.en: This company handles things in a very bureaucratic way.

examples.ko: 관료적인 태도 때문에 시민들이 불만이 많아요.
examples.en: Citizens have many complaints because of the bureaucratic attitude.

examples.ko: 절차가 관료적이라서 서류 하나 받는 데 한참 걸려요.
examples.en: The procedures are so bureaucratic that getting one document takes forever.
He talks in a stiff, bureaucratic way, so it's uncomfortable to chat with him.
Someone suggested changing the bureaucratic culture.

examples.ko: 너무 관료적으로 일하면 현장 문제를 놓쳐요.
examples.en: If you work too bureaucratically, you miss problems on the ground.

explain: 공무원이 아니어도 규칙과 형식만 따지고 융통성이 없는 방식을 비판할 때 써요. 대부분 부정적인 뉘앙스예요. 반대 느낌은 '유연하다', '융통성 있다'예요.
explain_en: You can use it even for non-civil servants to criticize a rigid, rules-and-forms-only way of working. It is mostly negative. The opposite feel is '유연하다' or '융통성 있다'.

examples.ko: 관료주의 때문에 간단한 일도 오래 걸려요.
examples.en: Because of bureaucracy, even simple things take a long time.

examples.ko: 우리 학교의 관료주의를 고쳐야 한다고 생각해요.
examples.en: I think our school's bureaucratic habits need to be fixed.

examples.ko: 관료주의가 심한 조직에서는 새 아이디어가 나오기 어려워요.
examples.en: In an organization with heavy bureaucracy, new ideas are hard to come by.
He got worn out by the bureaucracy and quit the company.
An article criticizing bureaucracy appeared in the news.
In class we discussed the problems of bureaucracy.

explain: 규칙과 절차, 윗선의 결정만 중요하게 여기는 조직 문화를 비판할 때 써요. 형용사처럼 쓰려면 '관료적'을 써요. 비슷한 비판으로 '탁상행정', '복지부동' 같은 말도 있어요.
explain_en: It is used to criticize an organizational culture that cares only about rules, procedures and top-down decisions. To use it like an adjective, say '관료적'. Similar criticisms include '탁상행정' and '복지부동'.

examples.ko: 주식 시장에서는 관망 분위기가 이어지고 있어요.
examples.en: A wait-and-see mood continues in the stock market.
I think waiting and watching is the best option right now.

examples.ko: 계속 관망만 하지 말고 이제 결정해요.
examples.en: Stop just watching from the sidelines and make a decision now.
Many people are still waiting to see how things go.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 관망 자세를 바꿔 투자를 시작했어요.
examples.en: That company dropped its wait-and-see stance and started investing.

examples.ko: 관망은 이제 그만하고 직접 해 봐요.
examples.en: Enough watching from the sidelines, let's try it ourselves.

explain: 어떤 일에 직접 끼지 않고 상황이 어떻게 되는지 지켜보는 것이에요. 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 '관망세', '관망 분위기'처럼 자주 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '지켜보다'라고 말하는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It means staying out of something and watching how the situation develops. In news and economy articles it often appears as '관망세' or '관망 분위기'. In everyday talk people often say '지켜보다' instead.

examples.ko: 우선 상황을 관망해 보고 결정하기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to watch how things go first and then decide.

examples.ko: 친구들 싸움을 옆에서 관망하기만 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't just stand by and watch your friends fight.
Investors are holding off until the interest rate announcement.
He stepped back and watched how the situation developed.
While I was waiting and watching, I missed the chance.

examples.ko: 좀 더 관망하면 답이 보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you wait and watch a bit longer, the answer will show up.

explain: '지켜보다'와 비슷하지만 직접 나서지 않고 형세를 살핀다는 느낌이 강해요. 때로는 소극적이라는 비판이 담기기도 해요. 경제 뉴스에서는 '관망하는 투자자'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '지켜보다' but has a stronger feel of not getting involved and just sizing up how things are going. It can sometimes carry criticism for being passive. In economic news you often see it as in '관망하는 투자자'.

examples.ko: 이 화분은 관상용이라서 물만 주면 돼요.
examples.en: This plant is just for display, so you only need to water it.

examples.ko: 거실에 관상용 식물을 몇 개 두었어요.
examples.en: I put a few decorative plants in the living room.
The fish I kept for display gave birth to young.
This flower is mainly ornamental, but it smells good too.
I went to the flower shop to buy an ornamental tree.
It's a fruit meant for looking at, not for eating.

explain: 먹거나 쓰려는 목적이 아니라 보고 즐기려고 기르는 식물이나 동물 앞에 붙여요. '관상용 식물', '관상용 물고기'처럼 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '식용'이에요.
explain_en: It goes in front of plants or animals that are raised to be looked at and enjoyed rather than eaten or used. You say things like '관상용 식물' or '관상용 물고기'. The opposite idea is '식용' (for eating).

examples.en: That greeting is an expression people use out of custom.
Try to break away from conventional ways of thinking.
These days most holiday greetings are just customary.
If you only use stock expressions, your writing gets boring.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 줄거리가 너무 관습적이라서 새롭지 않아요.
examples.en: This movie's plot is so conventional that it doesn't feel fresh.
Try finding an unconventional method.

explain: 오랜 습관이나 관례에 따라 하는 것을 말해요. '전통적'은 중립적이거나 좋게 들리지만, '관습적'은 생각 없이 틀에 박힌 대로 한다는 느낌이 담길 때가 많아요. 반대 느낌은 '독창적', '파격적'이에요.
explain_en: It describes doing something according to long-standing habit or convention. '전통적' sounds neutral or positive, while '관습적' often carries a feel of doing things by rote without thinking. The opposite feel is '독창적' or '파격적'.

examples.en: The flute and the trumpet are both wind instruments.

examples.ko: 저는 관악기 중에서 클라리넷을 배우고 싶어요.
examples.en: Among wind instruments, I want to learn the clarinet.

examples.ko: 관악기를 불려면 숨을 길게 쉬어야 해요.
examples.en: To play a wind instrument, you have to be able to breathe for a long time.
I joined my school's wind instrument club.
Wind instruments make sound when you blow into them.

examples.ko: 관악기 소리가 크게 울려서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The wind instruments rang out so loudly that I was startled.

explain: 바이올린 같은 '현악기', 북 같은 '타악기'와 함께 악기를 나눌 때 써요. 연주한다고 할 때는 '관악기를 불다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used together with '현악기' (string instruments such as the violin) and '타악기' (percussion such as drums) when classifying instruments. To say you play one, use '관악기를 불다'.

examples.ko: 우리 두 사람은 관포지교 같은 사이예요.
examples.en: The two of us are like a pair of truly close friends.

examples.ko: 관포지교라는 말처럼 진짜 친구는 어려울 때 알아요.
examples.en: As the old saying about Guan Zhong and Bao Shu goes, you know a true friend in hard times.
Their friendship is comparable to the legendary friendship of Guan and Bao.
It's reassuring to have a friend with whom I share such a deep bond.
The story behind this idiom comes from a Chinese tale.
We learned the story of Guan Zhong and Bao Shu's friendship in class.

explain: 중국의 관중과 포숙의 우정 이야기에서 나온 사자성어로, 서로를 깊이 이해하는 아주 가까운 친구 사이를 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화보다는 글이나 연설, 시험에서 더 자주 보이는 말이에요. '절친'이나 '죽마고우'와 쓰임이 조금 달라서, 이 말에는 서로의 처지를 알아주는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: This four-character idiom comes from the story of the Chinese friends Guan Zhong and Bao Shu, and is used for very close friends who deeply understand each other. It shows up more in writing, speeches and tests than in daily conversation. Unlike '절친' or '죽마고우', it carries a feel of understanding each other's situation.

examples.en: I'm going to an orchestral concert this weekend.
The orchestra played a piece by Beethoven.
Listening to orchestral music puts my mind at ease.

examples.ko: 그 작곡가는 관현악을 위한 곡을 많이 썼어요.
examples.en: That composer wrote many pieces for orchestra.

examples.ko: 관현악 편곡 덕분에 노래가 더 웅장해졌어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the orchestral arrangement, the song became more grand.
I was in an orchestra club in college.

explain: 관악기, 현악기, 타악기가 함께 연주하는 음악이나 그 편성을 가리켜요. 일상 대화에서는 '오케스트라'라고 더 많이 말하고, '관현악'은 '관현악단', '관현악곡'처럼 설명이나 공연 안내에서 자주 보여요.
explain_en: It refers to music played by wind, string and percussion instruments together, or to that kind of ensemble. In daily talk people more often say '오케스트라', while '관현악' appears in words like '관현악단' and '관현악곡' and in concert descriptions.

examples.en: He has a fiery temperament, so his voice is loud.
My grandmother has had a fiery personality since she was young.

examples.ko: 우리 이모는 말투가 괄괄하지만 마음은 따뜻해요.
examples.en: My aunt speaks bluntly and loudly, but she has a warm heart.
I like the way she laughs heartily.
The boss is straightforward and fiery.
If you have a fiery personality, people sometimes misunderstand you.

explain: 주로 사람의 성격이나 목소리가 거세고 활달할 때 써요. 같은 활발한 성격이라도 '시원시원하다'는 좋은 느낌이 강하고, '괄괄하다'는 거칠고 급한 느낌이 더 있어요. 주로 사람에게 쓰고, 칭찬보다는 성격을 묘사할 때 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is mostly used for a person's temperament or voice that is strong, rough and lively. Even among energetic personalities, '시원시원하다' sounds more positive, while '괄괄하다' adds a rougher, hastier feel. It is used mainly for people, more to describe character than to praise.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 괄목상대할 만큼 실력이 늘었어요.
examples.en: That student's skills have improved so much it's astonishing.

examples.ko: 몇 년 사이 도시가 괄목상대한 발전을 이뤘어요.
examples.en: In just a few years, the city achieved remarkable development.
This growth is a perfect fit for the phrase 'astonishing improvement.'
In just three months, he showed a dramatic change.
Our team's results have improved remarkably.
That player improved so remarkably that everyone was surprised.

explain: 한동안 못 본 사이에 실력이나 상황이 눈이 번쩍 뜨일 만큼 좋아졌을 때 써요. '괄목상대할 만한 성장'처럼 쓰고, 칭찬하는 말이라 나빠지는 변화에는 쓰지 않아요. 주로 글이나 뉴스, 연설에서 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: Use it when someone's skill or situation has improved so much since you last saw it that it makes you take a second look. It appears in patterns like '괄목상대할 만한 성장'. It is praise, so it isn't used for changes for the worse, and it appears mostly in writing, news and speeches.

examples.en: You shouldn't look down on people just because they are poor.

examples.ko: 그 가게에서 손님을 괄시해서 기분이 나빴어요.
examples.en: They treated customers coldly at that shop, so I felt bad.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 친척들에게 괄시를 많이 받았어요.
examples.en: I was treated with a lot of contempt by relatives when I was little.
Newcomers shouldn't be looked down on just for being new.
The disrespect was so bad that I was deeply hurt.
Please respect people instead of belittling them.

explain: '무시하다', '업신여기다'와 비슷한데, '괄시'는 상대를 푸대접하고 낮춰 대하는 행동까지 담겨 있어요. '괄시하다', '괄시를 받다/당하다'로 많이 써요. 비슷한 말로 '푸대접', '냉대'가 있어요.
explain_en: It is similar to '무시하다' and '업신여기다', but '괄시' also includes the act of treating someone poorly and as inferior. It is commonly used as '괄시하다' or '괄시를 받다/당하다'. Similar words are '푸대접' and '냉대'.
